\parbox{0.95\linewidth}{\footnotesize Each calendar quarter, all announcements are sorted into SUE quintiles. The treated portfolio buys treated (mega-cap day) announcements in the top quintile and sells those in the bottom quintile, holding each from trading day $+2$ to $+61$ after its reaction day, equal-weighted within each leg. The control portfolio does the same with the matched control announcements. Column (3) is the difference of the daily long-short returns. Days with fewer than 5 stocks on either side are dropped. Returns and alphas are in percent; $t$-statistics in parentheses use Newey-West standard errors with 10 lags; $^{*}$, $^{**}$, $^{***}$: 10\%, 5\%, 1\%. Break-even cost is the five-factor + momentum annual alpha divided by annual one-way turnover of both legs; n/a when the alpha is not positive. Factors: Ken French data library.}
